content:
[43011 Industrial Control System Security | Subject description]
Credit points: 6

This professional subject equips you with skills to protect critical infrastructures, like Industrial Control Systems (ICS) and Operational Technology (OT), from cyber threats. You will learn to identify vulnerabilities, assess risks, and implement security measures, including secure architectures and access controls. Your learning will be practical, involving lab exercises and real-world case studies, enabling you to defend against cyber-attacks on essential critical infrastructure systems.

[43011 Industrial Control System Security | Learning and teaching activities]
The subject will be delivered as a one-hour online lecture and a two-hour on-campus laboratory session every week. The learning and lab material are available in UTS Canvas. Students are expected to read the required textbook and study the learning material in their own time before the class.

The timetabled class will review industrial control system (ICS) security theories and designs that students have read about and/or watched videos prior to coming to class.

A collaborative learning environment is provided to enable students to work in teams and communicate their progress with peers and tutors during the semester. Continuous constructive feedback is provided in active learning so that students might make improvements during the semester and before submitting their final reports.

Students will learn the architectural principles, security threats, and key protection mechanisms for ICS environments. Students will also learn how to securely design, monitor, and defend ICS infrastructures against cyber threats. All material covered is assessable unless explicitly stipulated otherwise.

In the labs, students will practice security techniques and tools to protect industrial control systems from cyberattacks, unauthorised access, and system manipulation. The lab tasks include network segmentation, intrusion detection, access control mechanisms, incident response simulations, and secure communication protocols. In-class guidance and feedback on each report will be provided by tutors. Students will include the weekly advice and feedback in their due assessments.

title: Learning outcomes
content:
[43011 Industrial Control System Security | Learning outcomes]
SLO1: Differentiate key concepts in Industrial Automation to apply standards architecture in industry. (D.1)
SLO2: Apply various ICS security frameworks and standards to ensure security and to manage the industrial control system. (D.1)
SLO3: Analyse cyber threats and attack vectors to identify the vulnerabilities of ICS controls and enhance security in different scenarios. (D.1)
